text: Better know nothing than half-know many things! Better be a fool on one’s own account, than a sage on other people’s approbation!
plain: Go deep on your own, even if you look foolish. Borrowed wisdom is worth nothing.

text: Call me however what thou wilt—I am who I must be.
plain: Their labels don't change what you have to become.

text: Many a one have I found who stretched and inflated himself, and the people cried: ‘Behold; a great man!’ But what good do all bellows do! The wind cometh out at last.
plain: Hype and image fade. Whatever is just puffed up goes flat in the end.

text: O Zarathustra, everything is a lie in me; but that I collapse—this my collapsing is GENUINE!
plain: Even when you feel like a fraud, the way you break is real.

text: I love the great despisers. Man is something that hath to be surpassed.
plain: People who hate their small selves are the ones who grow past them.

text: Ah, he only who knoweth WHITHER he saileth, knoweth what wind is good, and a fair wind for him.
plain: Without a destination, no wind helps you. Know where you're going first.

text: ‘Nothing is true, all is permitted’: so said I to myself.
plain: Once you drop all rules, you have to build your own, and that's the hard part.

text: Too oft, verily, did I follow close to the heels of truth: then did it kick me on the face.
plain: Chasing the truth too closely gets you hurt. It's still worth it.

text: Thou hast lost thy goal. Alas, how wilt thou forego and forget that loss? Thereby—hast thou also lost thy way!
plain: Lose the goal and you lose the road. Keep the aim in front of you.

text: What still remaineth to me? A heart weary and flippant; an unstable will; fluttering wings; a broken backbone.
plain: At your lowest you can name exactly what is left, and start from that.

text: The least thing precisely, the gentlest thing, the lightest thing, a lizard’s rustling, a breath, a whisk, an eye-glance—LITTLE maketh up the BEST happiness.
plain: The best happiness is made of tiny things. Notice them.

text: There is nothing, O Zarathustra, that groweth more pleasingly on earth than a lofty, strong will: it is the finest growth.
plain: A strong will is the best thing a person can grow.

text: My arms and my legs, however, I do not treat indulgently, I DO NOT TREAT MY WARRIORS INDULGENTLY: how then could ye be fit for MY warfare?
plain: Go easy on yourself and you're not ready for the real fight.

text: I am a law only for mine own; I am not a law for all.
plain: Hold yourself to a hard standard without forcing it on everyone else.

text: And when I spake unto all, I spake unto none.
plain: Talk to everybody and nobody hears you. Aim at the few who matter.

text: The most careful ask to-day: “How is man to be maintained?” Zarathustra however asketh, as the first and only one: “How is man to be SURPASSED?”
plain: Don't ask how to stay safe and comfortable. Ask how to get past who you are now.

text: And rather despair than submit yourselves.
plain: Better to struggle and hurt than to give in and shrink.

text: He hath heart who knoweth fear, but VANQUISHETH it; who seeth the abyss, but with PRIDE.
plain: Courage means feeling the fear and looking into the drop anyway.

text: Do not will anything beyond your power: there is a bad falseness in those who will beyond their power.
plain: Don't claim more than you can deliver. Faking big goals makes you fake.

text: Take good care there, ye higher men! For nothing is more precious to me, and rarer, than honesty.
plain: Honesty is rare and valuable. Guard yours.

text: If ye would go up high, then use your own legs! Do not get yourselves CARRIED aloft; do not seat yourselves on other people’s backs and heads!
plain: Climb it yourself. Getting carried up means you can't hold the height.

text: In solitude there groweth what any one bringeth into it—also the brute in one’s nature. Thus is solitude inadvisable unto many.
plain: Being alone grows whatever you bring in, good or bad. Know what you're feeding.

text: The higher its type, always the seldomer doth a thing succeed. Ye higher men here, have ye not all—been failures?
plain: The harder the thing you're trying, the more often it fails. That's normal.

text: What wonder that many a vessel shattereth! Learn to laugh at yourselves, as ye ought to laugh! Ye higher men, O, how much is still possible!
plain: Of course you broke something. Laugh at it, a lot is still possible.

text: Set around you small, good, perfect things, ye higher men. Their golden maturity healeth the heart. The perfect teacheth one to hope.
plain: Surround yourself with small things done well. They heal you and give hope.

text: All great love doth not SEEK love:—it seeketh more.
plain: Real love isn't hunting to be loved back. It wants something bigger.

text: His step betrayeth whether a person already walketh on HIS OWN path: just see me walk! He, however, who cometh nigh to his goal, danceth.
plain: You can tell who's on their own road by how they move. Close to the goal, you move lightly.

text: Better, however, to be foolish with happiness than foolish with misfortune, better to dance awkwardly than walk lamely.
plain: If you're going to look dumb, do it while enjoying yourself. Move badly rather than not at all.

text: Ye higher men, the worst thing in you is that ye have none of you learned to dance as ye ought to dance—to dance beyond yourselves! What doth it matter that ye have failed!
plain: Failing doesn't matter. Not learning to go beyond yourself does.

text: Tortuously do all good things come nigh to their goal.
plain: Good things reach their goal by winding roads. A crooked path isn't a failed one.

text: Courage, however, and adventure, and delight in the uncertain, in the unattempted—COURAGE seemeth to me the entire primitive history of man.
plain: People got here by trying unknown things, not by hiding from them.

text: Ye have danced: a leg, nevertheless, is not a wing.
plain: A little progress isn't flight yet. Keep climbing.

text: Said ye ever Yea to one joy? O my friends, then said ye Yea also unto ALL woe.
plain: If you want one good moment, you accept all the pain that comes with it.

text: Do I then strive after HAPPINESS? I strive after my WORK!
plain: Don't aim for comfort. Aim at the work.

text: Even the pluckiest among us has but seldom the courage of what he really knows.
plain: Most of us know the hard truth and don't act on it.

text: Once for all I wish to be blind to many things.—Wisdom sets bounds even to knowledge.
plain: Ignore a lot on purpose. Knowing everything is not wise.

text: That which does not kill me, makes me stronger.
plain: Survive it and you come out stronger.

text: Help thyself, then everyone will help thee.
plain: Start moving yourself and others will join in.

text: A man should not play the coward to his deeds. He should not repudiate them once he has performed them. Pangs of conscience are indecent.
plain: Own what you did. Don't grovel over it afterward.

text: If a man knows the wherefore of his existence, then the manner of it can take care of itself.
plain: Know your why and you can put up with almost any how.

text: Thou seekest followers? Seek ciphers!
plain: Followers are zeros. If you want a crowd, expect nothing in it.

text: One should adopt only those situations in which one is in no need of sham virtues, but rather, like the tight-rope dancer on his tight rope, in which one must either fall or stand—or escape.
plain: Put yourself where there's no room to fake it. You stand or you fall.

text: Without music life would be a mistake.
plain: Keep something in your day that moves you. Without it everything goes flat.

text: A sedentary life is the real sin against the Holy Spirit. Only those thoughts that come by walking have any value.
plain: Get up and move. Your best thinking happens on your feet.

text: Art thou genuine or art thou only an actor?
plain: Are you the real thing or playing a part?

text: A man should know what he desires, and that he desires something.
plain: Know what you want, and be sure you want something.

text: They were but rungs in my ladder, on them I made my ascent:—to that end I had to go beyond them.
plain: Use things to climb, then leave them behind without apology.

text: To be obliged to fight the instincts—this is the formula of degeneration: as long as life is in the ascending line, happiness is the same as instinct.
plain: If you're constantly fighting yourself, something is off. Healthy drive pulls the right way.

text: I fear we shall never be rid of God, so long as we still believe in grammar.
plain: Old beliefs hide inside the way we speak and think.

text: The tragic artist is no pessimist,—he says Yea to everything questionable and terrible, he is Dionysian.
plain: The strong say yes to even the terrible parts of life.

text: A man is productive only in so far as he is rich in contrasted instincts; he can remain young only on condition that his soul does not begin to take things easy and to yearn for peace.
location: Morality as the Enemy of Nature 3
plain: Stay in tension and keep yearning for more. Chasing peace and ease makes you old.

text: The man who has renounced war has renounced a grand life.
location: Morality as the Enemy of Nature 3
plain: If you run from every fight, you give up a big life.
